page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-96GB is a shared-core cloud instance within the Cloud Native family, running on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 20 x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, operating with a single thread per core on a shared CPU allocation model. Cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. System memory totals 96.0 GB, yielding 4.8 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Hardware acceleration is absent with zero GPUs, and no local disk storage is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance trade-offs inherent to its shared-core execution model. Raw compute testing via stress-ng demonstrates top-tier single-core performance of 3506.58 points, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.64 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory writes are solid at 99.69 GB/sec. However, multi-core metrics settle into median ranges, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 58026.34 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12908. Memory subsystem results are mixed, with PassMark memory scoring in the bottom 25 percent at 1452.43 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression registering a weak 8.83 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and absence of bundled storage, this instance is structured around cost-efficient compute density rather than dedicated execution guarantees. The 96.0 GB memory footprint supports horizontal microservices, CI/CD compilation jobs, background queue handling, staging environments, and containerized orchestration where transient CPU bursting is acceptable. Workloads requiring strict latency determinism, intensive local NVMe I/O, or continuous sustained multi-core saturation may encounter resource throttling due to the non-dedicated CPU scheduling.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-96GB is a shared-core virtual instance equipped with 20 vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, built on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz under the KVM hypervisor. The CPU architecture features 16 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 instruction support, though execution resources are shared rather than dedicated. Hardware acceleration is absent, and no local storage is bundled. Benchmarks reflect outstanding single-core stress-ng performance in the top 10 percent, while multi-core compute, static web serving throughput (31.1 GB/sec), and Redis operations (32.43 million ops/sec) remain at average industry percentiles. PassMark memory metrics and single-threaded bzip3 decompression indicate bottlenecks in specific memory-intensive tasks. This configuration is aligned with cost-sensitive workloads requiring significant memory density and intermittent processing capacity, such as CI/CD pipelines, container clusters, and background task processing.
